extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, CRU/TC quality assurance staff, and reexamination clerks
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for USPTO examiners and support staff on concluding ex parte reexamination proceedings, preparing Notices of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificates, examiner's amendments, panel review conferences, publication preparation, and issuance of reexamination certificates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation review responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner is responsible for conducting a reasonable investigation for evidence as to whether the patent for which ex parte reexamination is requested has been or is involved in litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigation includes reviewing the reexamination file, the patent file, and results of the litigation computer search. If litigation or a federal court decision is discovered at any time, the examiner must bring the fact to the attention of the CRU SPRS or TC QAS prior to any further action; the CRU SPRS/TC QAS must review any action to ensure current Office litigation policy is followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal court decision controlling reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a federal court has ruled upon the merits of a patent and an ex parte reexamination is still appropriate, the federal court decision will be considered controlling as to claims finally held to be invalid by the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the court's decision with respect to claims finally held invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with PTAB review proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If a PTAB Review Proceeding (inter partes review, post-grant review, covered business method review) exists for the same patent, the Director may determine how the PTAB proceeding and the reexamination may proceed (stay, transfer, consolidation, termination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner becomes aware of a PTAB Review Proceeding for the same patent, the ex parte reexamination proceeding must be referred to the examiner’s SPRS. The SPRS will coordinate with the PTAB before taking action. The existence of a PTAB proceeding does not change the statutory three-month deadline for deciding a reexamination request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate (NIRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon conclusion of the ex parte reexamination proceeding the examiner must prepare a NIRC (form PTOL-469) and, if appropriate, an examiner's amendment; reasons must be given for each claim found patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must prepare the reexamination file so the Office of Data Management can prepare and issue a certificate under 35 U.S.C. 307 and 37 CFR 1.570; see MPEP § 2288 for certificate content. Examiner informs CRU SPRS/TC QAS of conclusion so panel review can be convened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review conference requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A CRU SPRS/TC QAS-convened panel review conference must be held to review the patentability of claims when the examiner concludes the reexamination proceeding, with conferees initialing the NIRC to indicate participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All conferees initial the NIRC even if one dissented. If the conference does not confirm the examiner’s decision, the examiner will reevaluate and issue an appropriate Office action rejecting the claim(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: When panel review is not required
rubrics_metrics.description: A panel review conference is not to be held as to any claim that was in the case at the time the case was reviewed by the Board or a federal court, and is not required where the proceeding is to be concluded by cancellation of all claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided: claims that were before Board/court at time of review are excluded from panel review; when all claims canceled, NIRC issuance is essentially ministerial and panel not needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIRC effect and limitations on further filings
rubrics_metrics.description: A NIRC informs the patent owner and any third-party requester that reexamination prosecution has been terminated; the rules do not provide for an amendment to be filed in a reexamination proceeding after prosecution has been terminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment, information disclosure statement, or other paper related to the merits filed after prosecution terminated must be accompanied by a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to have it considered. 37 CFR 1.312 does not apply in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of representative claim(s) for Official Gazette and certificate printing
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must indicate a representative claim and an appropriate drawing figure for printing on the certificate cover sheet and in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions: (A) select the broadest claim; (B) ordinarily designate one claim per invention (in reexamination select only one claim); (C) do not select a dependent claim unless the independent claim is also printed; for multiple dependent claims list the entire chain for one embodiment; in reexamination a dependent claim may be selected where the independent original has been canceled; in reissue select the broadest claim with changes or the broadest additional reissue claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue Classification IFW form completion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Issue Classification IFW form must be completed to set forth the status of each claim and the final claim numbers and to include the appropriate classification(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should enter the classification corresponding to current classification and any additional classification based on newly claimed subject matter. Current classification may be found using EAST/WEST. Completion is required even if all claims canceled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording claim selection and numbering on forms
rubrics_metrics.description: When recording representative claim(s) or claim numbers, enter claim numbers clearly; separate multiple claims by commas; refer to renumbered patent claim numbers rather than original claim numbers if different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure clarity and use renumbered claim numbers when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing attorney/agent names request
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner desires attorney/agent or law firm names printed on the certificate, a separate paper listing the names and positively stating they should be printed must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mere power of attorney or change of address is not a request that the name appear on the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of examiner checklist (PTO-1516) and clerk checklist (PTO-1517)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must complete form PTO-1516 for the reexamination file which will be forwarded to Office of Data Management; CRU support staff complete PTO-1517 and revise/update files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copy of form available from CRU SPRS or TC QAS. The clerk should check for changes in title, inventor, assignee, continuing data, foreign priority, attorney address, and requester address and ensure proper entry in file history and PALM. After clerk processing, files forwarded to CRU SPRS/TC QAS for review and approval prior to mailing NIRC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone contact before canceling all claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to canceling claims and issuing a NIRC because claims are to be canceled, the examiner should telephone the patent owner to inquire if a timely response or appeal was filed to ensure a timely response has not been misdirected within the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If patent owner indicates no timely filing or cannot be reached, examiner proceeds to issue a NIRC terminating prosecution. If owner was reached, the telephone interview will be made of record and attached to the NIRC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting examiner's amendment to cancel all claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When all live claims are canceled, the examiner will issue a NIRC and attach an examiner's amendment canceling all live claims; the amendment should point out why the claims have been canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of appropriate statements are provided, e.g., failure to timely respond referencing 37 CFR 1.550(d) and MPEP § 2266, or affirmation by Board decision with no timely appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of canceled/confirmed/amended/new claims in multiple dependency situations
rubrics_metrics.description: For multiple dependent claims, the addition of a claim of the multiple dependency is viewed as adding a new claim (protected subject matter); deletion of a claim of the multiple dependency is viewed as canceling that claim; for checklist purposes addition/deletion is viewed as amending the claim because of certificate printing conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate how claims are designated on Examiner’s checklist and the NIRC: confirmed (unchanged), amended (text changed or dependency changed), new (added protection), canceled (deleted). Printing shows amended form. Use renumbered claim numbers where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: All claims with a substantial new question (SNQ) must be examined
rubrics_metrics.description: All patent claims for which a substantial new question of patentability has been found must have been examined before concluding the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2243 for examination of claims with SNQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: No renumbering of patent claims is permitted (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: No renumbering of patent claims is permitted in reexamination; however, new claims may require renumbering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2250 for details on claim numbering and renumbering consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments must conform to 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j)
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments to the description and claims must conform to 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j), including examiner's amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a portion of the text is amended more than once, each amendment should indicate all of the changes (insertions and deletions) in relation to the current text in the patent under reexamination. See MPEP § 2250.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art listing forms requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior art must be listed on form PTO 892, PTO/SB/08A or 08B, or PTO/SB/42 (or a form equivalent in format).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These forms must be properly completed. See MPEP § 2257.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion and cross-checking of examiner and clerk checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner checklist PTO-1516 and reexamination clerk checklist PTO-1517 must be entirely and properly completed; clerical checklist is designed to check and review examiner’s responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRU support staff should personally review the file before completing items and ensure responses on both checklists are in agreement; careful reading of checklist instructions is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merging of multiple pending reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple pending reexamination proceedings are often merged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2283 for merger guidance and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copending reissue application coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Where reexamination is copending with a reissue application of the patent being reexamined, files must have been forwarded to OPLA for consideration of potential merger, with a Senior Legal Advisor decision present in the reexamination file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2285 for the forwarding and merger decision procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for patentability/confirmation required
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons for patentability and/or confirmation are required for each claim found patentable, unless all claims are canceled in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Box 2 of form PTOL-469 is checked and reasons provided as an attachment. The examiner should indicate why the claims are clearly patentable over the cited patents/printed publications, similar to reasons for allowance in an application (see MPEP § 1302.14). The reasons may be set forth on PTOL-476 or by using form paragraph 22.16. Examiner may refer to portions of the record which clearly establish patentability. Patent owner comments must be labeled and submitted promptly to avoid delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: No issue fee in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no issue fee in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2233.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims may not be amended or added after patent expiration
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent claims may not be amended nor new claims added after expiration of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2250. If the patent has expired during the proceeding, all amendments and added claims must be withdrawn; rejected/objected-to claims canceled by examiner's amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original drawings cannot be physically changed
rubrics_metrics.description: Original drawings cannot be physically changed; amended or new figures must be appropriately labeled and presented on new sheets in compliance with 37 CFR 1.84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.530(d)(3) and MPEP § 2250.01 for drawing amendment procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amended or new claim may not enlarge scope
rubrics_metrics.description: An amended or new claim may not enlarge the scope of the patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2250 for limits on amendments that would enlarge claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s amendment formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If examiner prepares an examiner’s amendment, it must comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j), including presentation of full text of any paragraph or claim to be changed with 37 CFR 1.530(f) markings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: an entire claim or paragraph may be deleted by a statement deleting the claim/paragraph without presenting the text. The exception for examiner’s amendments under 37 CFR 1.121(g) does not apply in reexamination proceedings. If examiner’s amendment is prepared, Box 7 of PTOL-469 is checked and form paragraph 22.06 is used to provide attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract changes require patent owner authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally title or abstract will not need changing; if necessary, patent owner should be notified to provide amendment early; if NIRC is or will be mailed, examiner may only change title/abstract by an examiner’s amendment authorized by the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing the title by merely initialing is not permitted in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement when patent expires during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent expires during reexamination, all amendments made during the proceeding are improper and must be expressly withdrawn by examiner’s amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner’s amendment should include an explicit withdrawal statement such as: 'As the patent being reexamined has expired during the pendency of the present reexamination proceeding, all amendments made during the proceeding are improper, and are hereby expressly withdrawn.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraph 22.06 for examiner's amendment attachment
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 22.06 is used as the examiner’s amendment accompanying the NIRC to show changes that will be reflected in the reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the specific examiner’s amendment text in the attachment area of the NIRC as provided by paragraph 22.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation language and categorization of claims (confirmed vs patentable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Original patent claims found patentable are generally designated 'confirmed' while new and amended patent claims are generally designated 'patentable'; examiner may use 'patentable' to refer to any claim that defines over the cited patents/printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no need to separate 'confirmed' and 'patentable' categories when setting forth reasons for patentability/confirmation. Where all claims are canceled, no reasons are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling submissions after NIRC (petition under 37 CFR 1.182)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules do not provide for amendment in reexamination after a NIRC; any amendment, IDS, or other paper related to merits filed after NIRC must be accompanied by a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 and the petition must be granted for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petition is granted, examiner will reconsider the case in view of new information and, if appropriate, reopen prosecution. See MPEP § 2256 for criteria for obtaining entry of IDS after a NIRC. 'Comments on Statement of Reasons' received will be placed in the reexamination file without comment, even if certificate already issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in ex parte reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The reexamination certificate must set forth the results of the proceeding and the content of the patent following reexamination and will: cancel any patent claims determined unpatentable; confirm any patent claims determined patentable; incorporate amended or new claims determined patentable; make any changes in the description approved; include statutory or terminal disclaimers filed by owner; identify unamended claims held invalid on final holding by another forum; identify any patent claims not reexamined; be mailed on its date to patent owner and a copy to requester; identify patent claims dependent on amended claims determined patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 35 U.S.C. 307 and 37 CFR 1.570 for statutory/regulatory bases. If a certificate cancels all claims, no further Office proceedings will be conducted regarding that patent. If reexamination concluded by grant of reissued patent, the reissued patent constitutes the certificate. Notice of issuance will be published in Official Gazette on date of issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of issuance of each reexamination certificate will be published in the Official Gazette on its date of issuance in a format similar to that used for reissue patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.570(f) and MPEP § 2291 for Official Gazette publication format and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special petition procedures when reexamination certificate cancels all claims but reissue copending
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reexamination certificate cancels all claims but a reissue application is copending, the patent owner may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 requesting waiver of 37 CFR 1.570(d) provisions to address claims pending in the reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must be accompanied by a paper cancelling any claim within scope of canceled claims and explaining why remaining reissue claims can be patentable despite cancellation by certificate. Such paper will be available to the examiner if petition granted. See 37 CFR 1.570(d).
